editorial.headline: Leaf Vegetable Farming as a Full Horticulture Chain
editorial.standfirst: A nationally open activity for growing edible leaves, stems, and flowers, with Bali PMA registration not blocked by the provincial moratorium note in this record.
editorial.body:
**KBLI 01131 covers leaf-vegetable farming as an integrated horticulture activity, not merely the act of planting greens in a field.** Its scope is the cultivation of vegetables whose leaves, flowers, or stems are eaten: artichoke, petsai or sawi, asparagus, cabbage, cauliflower, broccoli, lettuce, celery, leeks, spinach, and kangkung are all named in the record. The description also reaches other edible-flower, leaf, and stem vegetables within the same farming pattern.

The operational idea is a complete crop cycle. Land preparation, nursery or seedling work, planting, maintenance, harvesting, and post-harvest handling belong here when they are conducted as one connected chain. That matters because the code is framed around farming activity as a sequence, not a detached service. Spinach and kangkung harvested with their roots remain inside the scope. So do seed-oriented activities: planting leaf-vegetable crops to produce seed, plus nursery and seed-production work for leaf-vegetable horticulture.

On scale, the record is unusually straightforward. The activity is open to Mikro, Kecil, Menengah, and Besar, so it is not written only for a smallholder profile or only for a large agricultural company. A founder reading this code should understand it as a broad agricultural classification for leaf-vegetable production, capable of describing anything from smaller cultivation to larger organized farming, provided the activity remains within the scope stated above.

The national and Bali picture is also clean. Nationally, the PMA status is TERBUKA and the foreign ownership ceiling is 100%, sourced to Perpres 10/2021, 49/2021. Bali does have a province-wide moratorium rule that blocks all Low and Medium-Low risk KBLI for PMA, but this slim record does not mark the activity as blocked. Its Bali status is OK_or_HIGHER_RISK, with the reason stating that OSS risk at Besar scale is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi and therefore not blocked by the moratorium. In plain terms: for this record, a foreign-owned company can read the national door as open and the Bali moratorium note as not blocking PMA registration today.
